<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f9ef3f7951b312263e75a1b08a3c723fe218d4ff && git checkout f9ef3f7951b312263e75a1b08a3c723fe218d4ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99 0f6556d1c5c1cc53f73896f494dff140be5a0180 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99 && git merge --no-ff 0f6556d1c5c1cc53f73896f494dff140be5a0180

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9432bac077ecbfa703c09409f3fed416edd41d99` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0f6556d1c5c1cc53f73896f494dff140be5a0180`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22994 (body, triage `6121248027`, claim `6121395708` as edited, reports `6122651929` / `6123394404`, the ACCEPT `6123477244`, read as a claim); PR #23024 body, file list and the net diff against merge base `6a7eca6868` (4 files, +514 / -54); the 45 check-runs on this head (latest per name: 34 names, all concluded at the time of writing, 29 `success`, 5 `skipped` — Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in — 0 failed; `Check Changeset` was in progress on the first read and concluded `success` on the second); #14491 body and pointer `6122725038`; #15204 comment `6122715417`. Governing rules: AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12, Post-Task Checklist step 3, the clause ② definition in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ("a new key on a published payload") and the level paragraph in `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` ("a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface ... takes at least `minor`"). Code read at the head: `app-plugin.ts`, `artifact-collections.ts`, `metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts`, `spec/src/conversions/{apply,registry}.ts`, `plugin-sharing/src/bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts`, `plugin-security/src/bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts`, both test files.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. What the ObjectQL registry now holds, and every reader that moves with it — RIGHT.** `init()` hands `manifest.register` `this.forwardConverted(ctx).definition` whenever `this.bundle.packages === undefined`. `forwardConverted` memoizes one `applyArtifactForwardConversions` over `collections.manifest ? { ...manifest, ...collections } : collections`, with `collections = resolveArtifactCollections(this.bundle)`, which returns its argument by identity when `packages` is absent (`artifact-collections.ts`, the D7 branch). So the input is byte for byte the old `servicePayload`, and the registry decomposed over `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` now carries the converted copy of every collection. Readers that change, all through that one code layer: `readFlattenedMetaItems` on the `served` face (`GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE`, `protocol.ts:8786`) and the `execution` face (`getMetaItemsForExecution`, `:8814`), the email loader (which safe-parses the execution face), `readDeclared(ql, 'permission')` in the permission seeder, `readDeclared(engine, 'sharing_rule')` in the sharing seeder, and `readDeclaredCapabilityContext`. Every one moves toward the converted shape the item endpoint already serves on an artifact boot: on the conversion axis the list and item are now equal (the dashboard pin asserts one document); on the parse axis nothing moves (the registry copy still lacks the door's schema defaults — the email pin asserts subset, not equality, and the #14491 parse-axis pins are untouched). `_diagnostics.valid` flips `false` to `true` only for items the conversion rewrote, i.e. toward the item read's answer. No public answer moves in any other direction. The one reader class that now DIVERGES from the registry is AppPlugin's own raw readers (jobs, datasources, translations, `registerUnclaimedTopLevel`) — they read raw before and after, so nothing regresses, and #23029 carries them. RIGHT.

**2. An already-current bundle registers byte-identically — RIGHT.** `applyConversions` is copy-on-write per entry (each entry returns its input when it matches nothing), the two default flips are excluded by `DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE`, and `resolveArtifactCollections` is identity without `packages`. The control pin (`a current bundle is handed over unchanged`) asserts `toStrictEqual({ ...manifest, ...bundle })` and reference identity of the `dashboards` / `emailTemplates` arrays; the control boot asserts the registry holds exactly the authored items plus stamps. Test Core is green on this head. Note that this is the first time a `defineStack()` config boot (`os serve`, `DevPlugin`, verify's `bootStack`, embedders) replays the retired conversions over its NON-security collections; #12844 already ran the identical function on the identical bytes for the security collections of that boot, and the door runs it on every artifact boot, so no new policy is introduced — the same function, the same window verdicts. RIGHT.

**3. The authorization outcome — RIGHT, and `Clause-②: no` is the right line.** What I checked:
- The conversion that produces it is a declared ADR-0087 entry: `sharing-recipient-role-to-position` (`registry.ts:357`, protocol 13, ADR-0090 D3, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '15.0.0'`, "one-step rename, no alias window"), and the level is `sharing-rule-access-level-full-to-edit` (`registry.ts:878`, protocol 17, documented "strictly lossless: `full` never granted more than `edit`"). ADR-0087's chain record (step 13) names both. The #14491 fixture declares an `engines.protocol` range of greater-or-equal 17.1.0; floor 17.1.0 is below the 17.7.0 label, so the verdict is `converted-forward` and every retired entry replays — the same verdict the door already reached for the same bytes, which is why the pre-PR pins already read `position` / `edit` on the door copy.
- `mapRecipientType` is unchanged and still refuses `'role'`; nothing was made lenient at the seeder (Directive #12: no consumer alias, the conversion-layer entry does the work).
- The grant is not new to the platform's contract: `bootstrapDeclaredSharingRules` reads the registry first and falls back to `metadataService.list('sharing_rule')` only when the registry is empty (`:213`–`:219`), so on an engine-less composition the door's converted copy was ALREADY the seeder's input and this same declaration ALREADY seeded as a position share. The engine boot was the one composition dropping it. The PR makes the two compositions agree; it does not add a grant either of them promised to withhold.
- Against the Clause-② definition the gate mechanizes ("a new key on a published payload"; "a new exported symbol on an index, a new accepted key or value"): the diff adds no exported symbol (`forwardConverted` and `bootConversion` are private), accepts no new key or value anywhere, and moves no `packages/spec` schema. A seeded row that the declaration, the ADR-0087 entry and the door copy all already said should exist is enforcement catching up to the claim — Directive #10's "implement the rest", with the enforcement now exactly as wide as the declaration, not wider. Declaring it `yes (widening)` would assert a widening of a published accept set that does not exist, and demand a `minor` for it. `no`, bare, is correct; the operator-facing disclosure that a patch cannot carry in its level is carried by the changeset's sentence (judgment 6) and by this review, which the claim's widened ceiling owed for exactly this reason. RIGHT.

**4. One conversion per boot, ordering and source decisions — RIGHT.** `forwardConverted` is memoized on the instance and read at exactly two sites (`init()` and the registering branch of the security block in `start()`); `assertProtocolCompat(sys, …)` sits above the `servicePayload` ternary in `init()`, so the D1 handshake still runs first and a refused bundle never reaches the conversion. The one-conversion pin asserts identity (`toBe`) between the security registrar's registered object and the manifest payload's. #18034's `fromManifest` still reads `manifestSource` and `this.collections[field]`, the raw inputs; converting before the spread would strip `manifest.permissions` (`manifest-permissions-string-list-removed`) and void the "2 of 2" warning, so converting the spread is the right order and the #18034 pin is reported green. Under `securityMetadataRegistrar: 'artifact-door'` the block still registers nothing. A bundle carrying `packages[]` takes the raw branch unchanged (`{ ...manifest, ...bundle }`), leaving resolution to the `manifest` service per #15292; the security block for that shape converts `this.collections` exactly as before. Observation, not a finding: `packages: []` (present, empty) also takes the raw branch, since the test is `=== undefined`; whether the emitter produces that shape is not read here and belongs with #23027's routing. RIGHT.

**5. The five rewritten pins — RIGHT.** 13 `it(` before and after; no `skip` / `todo` / `only` in either file. Each keeps its subject and asserts more, not less: (1) `probe_agent` registry grant map now `toEqual` the exact four grants (which also pins the absence of the door's three defaults) and the RLS entry `toEqual` the door's whole entry without `priority`; (2) the stored `sys_permission_set` map still `not.toEqual` the door's (parse axis kept) while its RLS now equals the door's; (3) `share_legacy_deals` registry `sharedWith` and `accessLevel` equal the door's, `active` still absent on the registry copy; (4) `share_legacy_level` lands `edit` from the conversion rather than from `normalizeAccessLevel`; (5) the dropped rule is now asserted as one row with its full field set and `criteria_json`, seeded exactly once, three names where there were two. The diff touches only the header, the fixture comment and those five blocks; the Q2 `condition`, Q3 `scope`, #22203 position and row-shape pins are untouched. The header records the conversion/parse split. The dev's ablation (the one `init()` line) is reported to red exactly these five. RIGHT.

**6. The changeset's sentences against the diff — RIGHT, two nits.** Every sentence is true of the diff: the raw-bundle cause, the one conversion after the handshake, the identity return for a current bundle, the seeders reading the registry first, the `role` to `position` seeding, the dropped `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` / `priority`, and the `packages[]` case as unchanged. Nits, not errors: the headline says the list serves "the shape" the item serves, which is exact on the conversion axis and glosses the parse-axis defaults the item still carries (the PR body states that split precisely); and "hands its package bodies over as authored" understates the branch, which hands the whole bundle raw — moot in practice because the door refuses such an artifact at the package-body parse first (#23027). Neither misleads an upgrading agent grepping a retired key. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime` `patch` matches what the diff publishes: one published source file (`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`) with a behaviour fix, no new export, no new accepted key or value, no `packages/spec` change, no `index` widened; the tests and the changeset publish nothing. Post-Task step 3: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`. `Clause-②: no` is on PR body line 2, in the changeset body, and in the claim; the three agree; a bare `no` with no arm is a legal declaration (`no (widening)` would be malformed, and `yes` would owe `minor`). `check-adr-0087-registration` reports no declared-breaking changeset, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (who rewrites the five #14491 pins, and in which order against #22962)** — ruled A by the seat in the claim edit, executed in the patch round, verified in judgment 5. The file is `packages/runtime` (this lane); #14491's holder was told by pointer `6122725038`, #15204's lane by `6122715417` (whichever of #23024 and #22962 lands second merges `main` over one deleted block). Answered.
- **No dogfood test** (optional in the claim) — dogfood has no `@objectstack/runtime` dependency; the HTTP door was measured once and the new file boots the same composition in-package. Answered.
- **Email legs measured on #22990's head** — on this tree `category` / `isSystem` are live keys, so the email pins are positive controls here and reported 5-red-without / 8-green-with on `e4e96505e0`; the dashboard pins are the live falsifier on `main`. Answered; nothing here depends on #22990 landing.
- **The `packages[]` case** — left raw by design (#15292), stated in the PR body and the changeset, and the conversion layer's own miss on package bodies is filed as #23027 (`domain:engine`, p1, `pm:queue`). Answered by filing.
- **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` built 10 dists first** — a measurement prerequisite, exit 0 recorded. Answered.
- **PR body sentences the patch round made false** — the seat's ACCEPT says it corrected them; the body I read carries "357 of 357 files and 5141 tests" and the "(at `86d2782f09`, before the patch round …)" qualifier. Answered.
- **Out-of-scope findings** — #23027 filed; #23029 filed (`domain:cli`, p3) and its body records the translations note as not measured; the #14491 save-door member is the pointer on #14491. Two filed, two noted, as reported. Answered.
- Nothing escalated. The 29/5/0 check-run roster is the gate verdict on this head; Directive #14: no governed path in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success).
